title: Anticholinergic Cognitive Burden (ACB) scale - 2012 update, machine-readable
version: ACB 2012 update (Aging Brain Care, Regenstrief Institute / Indiana University); compiled 2026-10-10
compiledBy: MedWatch research (UnivaBio hackathon). Drug names, brands-as-printed and scores transcribed from the official card; RxNorm, brand verification and MedlinePlus links added programmatically.

categoryCriteria.1: Possible anticholinergic: in-vitro evidence that the chemical entity has antagonist activity at muscarinic receptors.
categoryCriteria.2: Definite anticholinergic: evidence from literature, prescribing information or expert opinion of a clinical anticholinergic effect.
categoryCriteria.3: Definite anticholinergic: evidence from literature, expert opinion or prescribing information that the medication may cause delirium.

scoringRules.numericScoring: Total ACB = sum of the scores of every medication the person takes; also count the number of possible and definite anticholinergic medications.
scoringRules.doseAndRoute: The scale is dose-independent and the card does not specify route; MedWatch scores systemic (oral/patch/injected) products only and lists topical/ophthalmic products as 'not scored' (MedWatch assumption).
scoringRules.combinationProducts: Score each anticholinergic ingredient of a combination product separately (e.g. Tylenol PM -> diphenhydramine 3).
scoringRules.duplicateIngredient: Count an ingredient once even if it appears in two products (MedWatch rule to avoid double counting; UNVERIFIED as an official ACB rule).

interpretation.claim: A total ACB score of 3 or more is associated with increased cognitive impairment and mortality; review risks, benefits and alternatives.

Compared with ACB = 0, people with total ACB >= 3 had adjusted hazard ratios of 1.83 (95% CI 1.53-2.20) for all-cause mortality and 2.17 (1.87-2.52) for incident cardiovascular disease over ~10+ years (EPIC-Norfolk, n=21,636).

Each additional definite anticholinergic (ACB 2-3) was associated with higher odds of incident cognitive impairment over 6 years (OR 1.46, 95% CI 1.07-1.99); possible anticholinergics (ACB 1) were not (OR 0.96).

Use of definite anticholinergics was associated with a 0.33-point greater 2-year MMSE decline (95% CI 0.03-0.64); 2-year mortality was higher with definite (OR 1.68) and possible (OR 1.56) anticholinergics.

The ACB card additionally states that each 1-point increase in total ACB has been correlated with a 26% increase in risk of death (citing Fox 2011); this figure is not in the Fox 2011 abstract and is UNVERIFIED against the full text in this session.
In hospitalised older adults, a dose-response relationship was seen between total ACB and cognitive impairment (Short Blessed Test).

Cumulative exposure to strong anticholinergics (antidepressant, antiparkinson, antipsychotic, bladder antimuscarinic, antiepileptic classes) was associated with increased dementia risk (highest exposure AOR about 1.49).

caveats: Associations are observational; a high ACB score is a prompt for medication review, not proof of harm in an individual.
The scale is dose-independent and does not capture newer drugs approved after 2012.
Different anticholinergic scales disagree on which drugs score and by how much (see alternativeScales).

alternativeScales.name: Anticholinergic Risk Scale (ARS)
alternativeScales.citation: Rudolph JL, Salow MJ, Angelini MC, McGlinchey RE. The anticholinergic risk scale and anticholinergic adverse effects in older persons. Arch Intern Med. 2008;168(5):508-513.
alternativeScales.summary: Ranked 0-3 categorical list; higher ARS scores were associated with more anticholinergic adverse effects in geriatric and primary-care cohorts.

alternativeScales.name: Anticholinergic Drug Scale (ADS)
alternativeScales.citation: Carnahan RM, Lund BC, Perry PJ, Pollock BG, Culp KR. The Anticholinergic Drug Scale as a measure of drug-related anticholinergic burden: associations with serum anticholinergic activity. J Clin Pharmacol. 2006;46(12):1481-1486.
alternativeScales.summary: 0-3 scale; scores associated with serum anticholinergic activity in long-term-care residents.

alternativeScales.name: CRIDECO Anticholinergic Load Scale (CALS)
alternativeScales.citation: Ramos H, Moreno L, Perez-Tur J, et al. CRIDECO Anticholinergic Load Scale: an updated anticholinergic burden scale. Comparison with the ACB scale in Spanish individuals with subjective memory complaints. J Pers Med. 2022;12(2):207.
alternativeScales.summary: 217 drugs (129 more than ACB); associated with cognitive impairment in a Spanish cohort where ACB was not.

alternativeScales.name: German Anticholinergic Burden Scale (GABS)
alternativeScales.citation: Kiesel EK, Hopf YM, Drey M. An anticholinergic burden score for German prescribers: score development. BMC Geriatr. 2018;18(1):239.

alternativeScales.name: Systematic review of 19 scales
alternativeScales.citation: Lisibach A, Benelli V, Ceppi MG, et al. Quality of anticholinergic burden scales and their impact on clinical outcomes: a systematic review. Eur J Clin Pharmacol. 2021;77(2):147-162.
alternativeScales.summary: 19 scales identified; ACB and GABS rated highest quality; findings for delirium, cognition, mortality and falls were contradictory across studies.

alternativeScales.name: AGS Beers Criteria 2023 Table 7
alternativeScales.summary: Not a score: a list of drugs with strong anticholinergic properties; Beers recommends avoiding combinations of >=2 anticholinergic drugs (risk of cognitive decline, delirium, falls/fractures).
